questions.question: Explain image sampling and quatization.
questions.solution_html: • Explain image sampling and quantization. /[CO1] Image sampling (1 mark) : Sampling converts the continuous spatial coordinates of an image into a finite set of discrete pixel locations. Image quantization (1 mark) : Quantization converts the continuous intensity values of the sampled image into a finite number of discrete intensity or gray levels.

questions.question: Analyze the effect of dilation on an object.
questions.solution_html: • Analyze the effect of dilation on an object. / [CO3] Dilation is a morphological operation that expands or thickens foreground objects' boundaries in an image using a structuring element. — (1 mark) . Can connect nearby objects, fill small gaps or bridge narrow breaks, depending on the structuring element — (1 mark) .

questions.question: State the objectives of histogram equalization. Explain how it improves the contrast of a low-contrast image.
questions.solution_html: • State the objectives of histogram equalization. Explain how it improves the contrast of a low-contrast image. Objectives of histogram equalization (3 marks) , Histogram equalization improves its contrast through the following steps: Calculate the histogram: Determine the frequency of each intensity level in the image. Compute the cumulative distribution function (CDF): Calculate the cumulative sum of the normalized histogram values.Transform pixel intensities: Use the CDF to map the original intensity values to new values distributed across a wider intensity range.
